title: fix(security): the single-posture platform-admin grant is owned by the Default Organization, and every reader of platform standing reads it
body:
Fixes #11979
Part of #15212
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

C8 stage 8b-0a (plan 6251466182 on #15212). Under the `single` tenancy posture the first-user platform-admin promotion keeps its zero-config behaviour, and the `admin_full_access` grant row it writes is now **owned by the Default Organization** (ADR-0131 D5, maintainer ruling A on #18707). Every reader of platform standing reads that row beside the organization-less one. The walled posture is unchanged.

## What changes

1. **The promotion writes the Default Organization** (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`). The grant carries `organization_id` = the Default Organization: `slug = 'default'`, else the only organization. That is plugin-auth's boot-invariant definition, resolved through the module's existing `resolveDefaultOrganizationId`. A deployment that names no Default Organization (several organizations, none `default`) is not promoted. It logs one `error` line and returns `reason: 'default_organization_unresolved'`, and writes no grant without an owner. The holder scan (leg A, and the predicate legs B and C apply) reads the Default Organization's grant and the organization-less one. A user holding both is one holder, and whichever row sorts first by `id` answers.
2. **The resolver's anchor is one predicate with the posture as its parameter** (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`). `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding(grant, { walled, defaultOrganizationId })`: under a wall nothing anchors (unchanged); under `single` the Default Organization's grant and the organization-less row anchor. The anchoring grant applies in whichever organization the principal acts in, as the organization-less row always did. Any other organization's grant of the set confers the set, never standing. `sys_organization` is read only for a principal holding an organization-owned `admin_full_access` grant under `single`, so the batch-equivalence goldens do not move.
3. **plugin-auth reads the same row** (`ensure-default-organization.ts`). The grant anchor reads the Default Organization's grant. Under `single`, step 4 reuses the Default Organization by the invariant's definition (a sole organization with another slug included) instead of minting a second, `default`-slugged one that would take the anchor off the promoted grant. Under a wall only the `default`-slugged one is reused, as before.

4. **The extra `sys_organization` reads, and when they run.** The resolver reads it only under `single`, and only for a principal holding an organization-owned `admin_full_access` grant: one small indexed read when a `default`-slugged organization exists, two otherwise, per uncached request (deduplicated within a request; the cross-request grants cache is off by default). Every other principal reads nothing more, which is why the batch-equivalence goldens (whose fixture holds the organization-less row) do not move. The last-administrator guard adds one or two reads per enumeration whenever an `admin_full_access` grant names an owner, so about three to six small reads per guarded write on `sys_user`, `sys_member`, `sys_user_permission_set`, the activation ledger and `sys_organization`.

### Landing points outside the claim's file surface, and why

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts` is the break-glass guard. Its enumeration, its "emptied rather than fresh" evidence reads and its switched-off-set read all keyed on `!organization_id`. Left alone, the promoted admin's grant would count as no administrator, and the guard would wave through the ban or revocation that ends the last one. It now reads the anchor the resolver reads. Because the anchor now depends on `sys_organization`, it also judges the two organization writes that move it: changing the Default Organization's `slug` while another organization exists, and deleting it.
- `packages/core/src/security/admin-standing-surface.ts` gains `sys_organization` as a `derives` table (columns `id`, `slug`, measured by `admin-standing-surface.test.ts`). The f8eb73601 correspondence gate turned red without it, and is green with the guard's new standing-key list.
- No ceremony file is touched. A3 below shows the ceremony's attribution is the intended D10 fate. The fix is on the readers' side.

## A3 — measured: the ceremony attributes the promoted admin's grant to the Default Organization

On `18.0.0-next.3` semantics (this branch's base `e4bcced0`), with the cli acceptance fixture of `organization-ownership-apply.test.ts` plus one promoted-admin grant (`grant_admin`, `organization_id` NULL, `permission_set` `admin_full_access`). This was a scratch copy of the fixture run under `--project integration` and deleted afterwards:

```
A3-READING [["attribution","done"], …] [{"id":"grant_admin","user_id":"usr_admin","permission_set":"admin_full_access","organization_id":"org_default"}]
```

So after `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` the grant is the Default Organization's. On the base tree that row conferred nothing. The resolver read `!ownGrant` only: the new `[ADR-0131 D5]` resolver tests fail on base (2 of 6). And the holder scan found no NULL holder and promoted again: the new fresh-boot golden "an upgraded database whose administrator's grant the ceremony gave the Default Organization promotes nobody else" fails on base and passes here. That is the live defect the dispatch suspected. The `rewrite` step blocked in that scratch run only because the fixture's catalog double serves no `admin_full_access`, which has nothing to do with attribution.

## Tests

On the final head `bc90a53af6` (after merging `origin/main`):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test`: 104 files, 2558 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: 188 files, 3739 passed, 45 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: 162 files, 3140 passed, 10 skipped.
- `typecheck` for core, plugin-security and plugin-auth: exit 0 (plugin-auth after its build, which its examples project reads).
- Platform-admin dogfood (`packages/qa/dogfood`, on a full build): `admin-platform-admin-standing`, `org-admin-affordance-reach` and `admin-credential-lifecycle` pass, 26 tests. The boot log shows `first user promoted to platform admin: admin@objectos.ai` three times and no withheld promotion.

New or flipped pins assert the substance:
- the fresh-boot golden's grant owner `null` becomes `org_default`;
- an attributed grant is a holder, and nothing is re-promoted;
- a database naming no Default Organization withholds at `error` and writes nothing;
- the resolver confers standing from the Default Organization's grant, in it and with no active organization, and from a sole organization of any slug, but not from another organization's grant, not with several organizations and none `default`, and never under a wall, which reads no organization;
- the guard counts the holder and refuses the ban, the revocation, the re-scoping, the re-slugging and the delete; the controls are another organization's grant and a sole organization's slug or name change;
- `ensureDefaultOrganization` binds the Default Organization's grant holder.

The test fixtures that promote now hold the Default Organization the `single` boot creates.

**Reverse verification.** The fix was committed first. The four source files were then restored to base `e4bcced0` and the new tests run, and the files restored to HEAD (proved by an empty `git diff HEAD` and HEAD-blob hash equality). Results on base: core D5 suite 2 failed; plugin-security fresh-boot golden 3 failed; plugin-auth guard and default-org suites 7 failed. All green on HEAD.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 73 families at `11016ab9`. All 73 ran with exit 0 after a full build (`check:i18n` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET before it, and green after). `--ran` reconciliation: "73 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 73 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)". The derivation is unchanged on the final head. A subset (`check:published-files`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:doc-authoring`) was re-run after the last source commit, all exit 0. Every family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- Clause-②: yes (narrowing). Breaking, shipped as `minor` on all three packages under the launch-window convention; the changeset carries the three FROM → TO pairs with their fixes and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Narrowings: (1) plugin-security — a `single` deployment with several organizations and none slugged `default` is no longer promoted (one `error` line, `reason: 'default_organization_unresolved'`, no row); fix: slug the intended organization `default`. (2) plugin-auth — a `sys_organization` `slug` change or delete that would leave no administrator who can sign in is refused (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`); fix: give another account administrator standing first. (3) plugin-auth — `ensureDefaultOrganization` under `single` reuses a sole organization of any slug instead of creating a second `default`-slugged one. Widening: under `single` a Default-Organization-owned `admin_full_access` grant now confers `PLATFORM_ADMIN` and applies in every organization (a pre-existing Default-Organization-scoped grant gains the rung on upgrade), and `sys_organization` becomes a standing-deriving table. No spec, REST answer or package entry changes: the new core helpers and the guard's organization key list are module-private; the bootstrap's return gains one `reason` string.
- Line budget: the dispatch estimated about 200 source lines. This lands about 620 source lines and 425 test lines. The extra source is the break-glass guard (enumeration, evidence reads, organization hooks), which the anchor change made necessary, plus its explanatory comments.
- Not in this PR: the organization-less reader's retirement (stage 8c-2) and engine-wide system-insert stamping (stage 8b). The organization-less row still anchors under `single`, by D5's "until D10's migration clears it".
- #11979's Constraints paragraph ("config now required for admin") is superseded by ruling A, as the card's discharged note says. Nothing here requires config under `single`.
